issues.body: The canonicalisation bullet says: "share the existing `sparq-canon` serialization and scope-canonicalisation primitives where the frozen profile permits". No scope-canonicalisation primitive exists in the crate today — `crates/sparq-canon/src/lib.rs` exports only whole-dataset/whole-graph entry points (canonicalize_quads, canonicalize_quads_with, digest_quads_with, issue_quads, canonicalize_triples, …), and the token "scope" does not appear anywhere in `crates/sparq-canon/src/`. The same document contradicts the new sentence twice: §4 ends with "**Gap:** there is no scope-extraction primitive. `sparq-canon` canonicalizes what it is handed; it has no notion of a node neighbourhood or an SCC", and §6 phase 2 lists "Scope-canonicalization primitive in `sparq-canon` (feature-gated, default-off)" as future, gate-blocked work. Describing planned work as existing is the kind of drift this record was written to prevent — a future implementer reading §9 alone would expect an API that is not there.
issues.fix_hint: Reword to distinguish what exists from what is planned, e.g.: "share the existing `sparq-canon` serialization primitives, and the scope-canonicalisation primitive planned in §6 phase 2, where the frozen profile permits…".
issues.title: §9 calls sparq-canon's scope-canonicalisation primitives "existing"; they do not exist and §4/§6 say so

issues.body: §9's PKG/vector bullet lists the reusable key as `(concept multihash, model id, model version, content version, verbalisation regime, metric, normalization, dimension)` and then asserts "Those latter axes already exist in `EmbeddingProvenance`". Six of the seven do (`model_id`, `model_version`, `content_version`, `verbalization`, `metric`, `normalization` — crates/sparq-vectors/src/spqv_provenance.rs:169-189), but `dimension` does not: the rustdoc at spqv_provenance.rs:162-164 states "`dim` is NOT stored here (it is already the store's header dimension and checked there); the compatibility check folds the store dimension in", and `to_rdf` takes `dim` as a caller-supplied parameter precisely because it is not a field (spqv_provenance.rs:287-292). The substantive argument (incompatible coordinate spaces must not collide under one concept hash) is unaffected, but the sourcing sentence is inaccurate as written.
issues.fix_hint: Amend to note that dimension is carried by the store header rather than by `EmbeddingProvenance`, and is folded in by `EmbeddingProvenance::compatible_with` at the store level — so the full key spans provenance plus the store header.
issues.title: `dimension` is claimed to be an EmbeddingProvenance axis, but it is deliberately not stored there

issues.body: §3.2 and §7 record closure as unresolved: "Whether the frozen profile mandates closure, and what a verifier does with a non-closed record, is open question **Q2**", with fail-closed given only as sparq's default reading. §9 now asserts "blank-node closure must therefore be a profile invariant, not an implementation convenience". Read as sparq's recommended answer to Q2 this is coherent and well-argued, but read in isolation it looks like the open question has been settled inside this repo — which it has not, since Kern/PSS own the profile.
issues.fix_hint: Add an explicit pointer, e.g. "… must therefore be a profile invariant (this is sparq's recommended resolution of open question **Q2**, §3.2/§7 — not an agreed decision)".
issues.title: §9 states blank-node closure "must be a profile invariant" without cross-referencing open question Q2

issues.body: "The ZK estate remains research-grade and lacks the pending external audit." is an honest, correctly hedged caveat and passes the honesty posture. Elsewhere the repo consistently names the tracking gate for this claim — scripts/check-privacy-claims.sh headers it as "sq-qhy4 (the ZK-soundness external-audit gate)" — so a bare mention here is slightly harder to trace than the house convention. Also, the phrase "lacks the pending external audit" reads awkwardly.
issues.fix_hint: Reword to the canonical form, e.g. "The ZK estate remains research-grade: the v1 verifier is not externally audited and external accredited-cryptographer sign-off is still pending (`sq-qhy4`)."
issues.title: ZK not-yet-audited caveat omits the sq-qhy4 gate reference used elsewhere in the repo

verdict.summary: Doc-only change: adds §9 "Estate-fit verdict from the earlier KB evaluation" (sq-y64lh / issue #3124) to research/genai-urn-concept-verifier-design.md. No crates/, tests, or gates touched, so there is no test-validity or runtime-security surface. I verified the load-bearing factual claims against the checkout: (a) the ZK description is accurate — crates/sparq-zk/src/commit.rs computes C(G) as a Poseidon2 sponge over leaves in canonical N-Quads order with a length-bearing IV for per-leaf-count domain separation, and scheme IRIs come from crate::registry (ZK_SCHEME_POSEIDON2_*); BN254/Poseidon2 is the documented field/permutation (lib.rs:6-12); (b) the .spqv graph-generation/staleness contract exists (skills/vector-search/SKILL.md:96-107); (c) §9's summary of §3 (whole-dataset RDFC-1.0 output cannot serve as a concept identifier) is a faithful restatement; (d) the closing paragraph is consistent with §1/§8 — nothing is consumed and no EmbeddingProvenance semantics are reserved ahead of the freeze. The ZK paragraph carries an explicit not-externally-audited caveat, so the privacy-claims honesty gate posture is satisfied (research/** is path-excluded from scripts/check-privacy-claims.sh in any case). No hard-coded performance numbers; the [GPT-5.6] provenance marker matches the established convention in research/. Two minor accuracy defects remain — one primitive described as "existing" that the same document elsewhere records as a gap, and one provenance axis (dimension) that is not in fact an EmbeddingProvenance field — plus two nits. None are blocking for a design record whose surrounding sections already state the correct position, so I approve with the findings noted for a follow-up doc pass. Completeness against the original issue #3124 ask could not be verified from the checkout (sq-y64lh is not present in .beads/issues.jsonl and no network access was used).
